text: The present 15 m white masonry tower on the beach was first lit in 1907. It replaced a 33 m stone tower built here in 1847. Source: Wikipedia, Kozhikkode Lighthouse.

The family temple of the Zamorins of Calicut, in its present form from the 14th century, built in the traditional Kerala style. It was badly damaged during Tipu Sultan's invasion in the 18th century and renovated in 1964. Source: Wikipedia, Tali Shiva Temple.

Built in the 14th century by Nakhuda Mishkal, a merchant and shipowner active in Calicut in the 1340s. The Portuguese burned it in 1510; rebuilt in 1578, it now has four storeys of timber with tiled roofs and no domes or minarets, beside the Kuttichira tank. Source: Wikipedia, Mishkal Mosque.
The large tank at the heart of the old city, beside Mananchira Square.
Road bridge in the heart of the city carrying Bank Road over the railway to Beach Road. Source: Onmanorama, August 2023.

The 28.4 km six-lane stretch of NH 66 between Ramanattukara and Vengalam keeps through traffic out of the city. It has seven flyovers, at Ramanattukara, Azhinjilam, Pantheerankavu, Palazhi, Thondayad, Pooladikunnu and Vengalam, and overpasses at Malaparamba and Vengeri. Sources: The Hindu, Onmanorama (2025).
